items.title: Simple modules over a finite algebra
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma collects basic facts about modules over a finite algebra: there is a simple module, every nonzero module has a simple submodule, a simple module is finite dimensional, and the endomorphism ring of a simple module is a skew field (statement lines 336-346). The proof is a complete argument: the first assertion follows from the second because the algebra is a nonzero module over itself, and the second holds by taking a submodule of minimal finite dimension, whose existence is guaranteed by cyclicity (proof lines 348-351); finite dimensionality of a simple module follows from the submodule generated by an element (proof lines 352-353); and a nonzero endomorphism of a simple module is injective and hence an isomorphism, which makes its endomorphism ring a skew field (proof lines 353-354). The non-formal content is the minimal dimensional submodule argument. The claim is H2.
